raw.product_description: Narma is an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" designed for AI-first companies. It comprises three layers: Observe (lightweight desktop sensors capture work patterns like application usage, activity sequences, and time allocation), Intelligence (a "Brain" that detects employee intent, business value of tasks, and "drift"), and Execution (an "Agent Factory" that automatically generates, deploys, and monitors AI agents for validated high-ROI opportunities with built-in approval gates). The system leverages existing foundation models and focuses on understanding the "Work Graph" to identify AI intervention points.
raw.evidence_of_stage: The venture is described as a concept and architecture, with no mention of development, users, or revenue.
raw.thesis: Narma is developing an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" to enable AI-first companies to implement and scale AI automation effectively. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an Observe layer for capturing work patterns, an Intelligence layer for detecting intent and identifying high-ROI automation opportunities, and an Execution layer for automatically generating and deploying AI agents. This system is designed to provide continuous AI lift by observing work, deciding on AI interventions, and automating agent development. Narma targets AI-first companies that struggle with quantifying AI savings, measuring ROI, and managing process drift. It aims to replace the current fragmented approaches to AI automation with a unified system that proves and scales the value of AI. The venture appears to be at the idea stage, focusing on establishing the concept and architecture. The founder’s goal is likely a growth startup, given the ambition to provide an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for "AI-first companies" which implies significant scale and impact.
